title: Fourth-moment recurrence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number. For each $i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, let $\Omega_i$ be a finite set with probability mass function $p_i$, and let $X_i:\Omega_i\to\bbr$. Let $a$ assign real coefficients to subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. If $X_0$ has mean zero and third moment zero under $p_0$, then the fourth moment of the associated multilinear random variable under the independent product distribution is the sum of three terms: the fourth moment of $X_0$ times the fourth moment of the polynomial formed from coefficients whose subsets contain $0$; six times the second moment of $X_0$ times the expected product of the squares of the polynomials formed from subsets containing and omitting $0$; and the fourth moment of the polynomial formed from subsets omitting $0$. Each polynomial in these terms uses the remaining coordinates and their corresponding functions $X_i$.
